answer: Cross-Identity Forfeit Ledger. Each operator registers a public ledger address; every wallet it controls cites that address at creation. If any one wallet is proven fake, the ledger debits the operator's posted collateral and freezes all its wallets—so a clone costs the operator the whole fleet, not a marginal fee. Reputation posts as a lagoon marker; collateral held in shale escrow; forfeiture recorded as an opal entry. Attackers must over-collateralize every identity at fleet scale.
